title: Seitan vs. tofu vs. tempeh: nutrition compared

seo.title: Seitan vs. tofu vs. tempeh: protein and calories
seo.meta_description: Compare seitan, firm tofu and tempeh per 100 g for protein, fat, calories, calcium and sodium—and see why processing matters.
seo.search_intent: Compare the nutrition of seitan, tofu and tempeh

excerpt: Seitan, tofu and tempeh can fill the same spot on a plate, but they are nutritionally different: seitan is concentrated wheat gluten, tofu is soybean curd, and tempeh is fermented whole soybeans.
content_html:
Seitan, tofu and tempeh are often grouped together as plant proteins, but they are made very differently. Seitan is mostly cooked wheat gluten, tofu is coagulated soy milk, and tempeh ferments whole soybeans.

Side by side per 100 g

Per 100 gSeitanFirm tofuTempeh
Calories~158144192
Protein~31.6 g17.3 g20.3 g
Fat~0.9 g8.7 g10.8 g
Carbohydrate~8.8 g2.8 g7.6 g

Seitan is the most protein-concentrated in this comparison, but the other foods bring different nutrients and textures.

Tofu calcium depends on the coagulant

The USDA firm tofu reference is made with calcium sulfate and contains about 683 mg calcium per 100 g. Tofu made mainly with magnesium salts can be much lower.

Tempeh is a denser whole-soy food

Tempeh keeps the soybean structure and provides about 20 g protein/100 g along with about 11 g fat. It is also more calorie-dense than many tofu products.

Seitan can be surprisingly high in sodium

The product used here lists 440 mg sodium per 57 g, roughly 770 mg/100 g. Other brands can differ substantially because sodium comes largely from the recipe.

Which one makes the most sense?

Seitan is efficient when protein is the priority and gluten is not a problem. Tofu offers protein plus unsaturated fat and potentially meaningful calcium. Tempeh combines concentrated soy protein with a chewy fermented-bean matrix.

faq.question: Which has the most protein?
faq.answer: In these references, seitan at about 31.6 g/100 g, versus 20.3 g for tempeh and 17.3 g for firm tofu.

faq.question: Is tofu always high in calcium?
faq.answer: No. Calcium varies with the coagulant.

faq.question: Is seitan gluten-free?
faq.answer: No. It is made primarily from wheat gluten.

faq.question: Is tempeh higher in calories than tofu?
faq.answer: In these references, yes: about 192 vs. 144 calories per 100 g.
